route: explicit code labels in the S4 Table Code Book, disambiguated against the rival S3 Table questionnaire numbering by keying polarity (route 6), a marker item (route 7) and don't-know rates on the swapped pairs; per-item n re-derived from the raw S5 file; re-runnable as verify_carver_2017_puggs_pilot1_det_core.R
evidence: Code-label tie: the S4 Table Code Book's Section 2 Part 2 lists 'Variable/Question' 1..13, each a distinct statement, and the S5 raw file's data columns are literally Q1..Q13, which data/carver_2017_puggs_items.py melts with var_name='item', so item Qk IS column Qk -- no positional or order inference. THE RISK this route had to close: the S3 Table questionnaire numbers the SAME 13 statements in a DIFFERENT order (permutation S3->CodeBook = 1->2, 2->7, 3->4, 4->10, 5->5, 6->12, 7->3, 8->8, 9->11, 10->1, 11->9, 12->6, 13->13; only 5, 8, 13 fixed), so 'explicit code labels' alone does not identify which document the data honours, and picking wrong mis-words 10 of 13 items while passing every set gate. Identity of source: applying the script's filter (keep 1-4, drop don't-know 5 and missing 99) to the raw S5 columns reproduces the live per-item n exactly for all 13 items (Q1 200/200, Q2 185/185, Q3 205/205, Q4 191/191, Q5 131/131, Q6 194/194, Q7 148/148, Q8 189/189, Q9 168/168, Q10 185/185, Q11 205/205, Q12 173/173, Q13 183/183; live n from irw_table_sets(per_item=TRUE), no export). Discriminator 1 (keying polarity, route 6): the Code Book marks each statement true or false, and the false ones are the determinism-positive ones; the two numberings key Q2 and Q4 OPPOSITELY, and item-rest correlation against the determinism-keyed mean of the other 12 gives Q2 +0.063 (Code Book) vs -0.135 (S3) and Q4 +0.126 vs -0.142, i.e. both invert under S3 numbering; whole-scale mean item-rest r 0.131 vs 0.040. Discriminator 2 (marker item, route 7): the lifestyle/diabetes statement is the block's one near-consensus item and lands at Q3 -- mean 3.78, 161 of 205 at 'strongly agree', 0 'strongly disagree', 1 'don't know' -- exactly where the Code Book puts it, while S3 numbering would put it at Q7, whose observed distribution is mean 2.16, 3 'strongly agree', 19 'strongly disagree', 55 'don't know'. Discriminator 3 (don't-know rate on the swapped pair {Q9,Q11}): the long technical amino-acid/protein statement draws 39 'don't know' at Q9 against 2 at Q11; the Code Book puts the technical statement at Q9 and the easy 'most traits and diseases are caused by both genes and environmental factors' at Q11, S3 numbering reverses it, and a technical item cannot draw 2 don't-knows while the trivial one draws 39. Option axis (route 9 in spirit): resp 1-4 = Strongly disagree..Strongly agree per the Code Book, and the direction is confirmed rather than assumed -- the consensus true statement Q3 sits at mean 3.78 of 4 with 79% at resp 4. NOT ESTABLISHED: the tested candidate space is the two numberings the deposit actually publishes, not all 13! permutations; discriminator 1 separates the two documents only at Q2 and Q4, discriminators 2 and 3 only at the swapped pairs {Q3,Q7} and {Q9,Q11}, and the remaining positions rest on the Code Book's explicit numbering against the S5 column names rather than on these statistics. The block's internal consistency is genuinely weak (the paper reports this for the first pilot) and Q1 has a mildly negative item-rest r under both numberings, so polarity is read only where the rivals disagree. Nothing here tests the Brazilian Portuguese wording actually administered, which the deposit does not publish, nor the instructions text, which exists in only one version (S3).

route: route 8 (non-response semantics) + exact per-item n reproduction from the raw S5 Table
evidence: Route 8 (semantic coherence of the non-response pattern), decisive. The pilot's Section 3 is published twice under two DIFFERENT numberings of the same 18 statements -- SI 3 (initial questionnaire) and SI 5 (Code Book) -- so the whole mapping turns on which one the columns Q14..Q31 follow. 'Don't know' was an offered option dropped upstream, so per-item n is a non-response measure. Exactly five stems contain the jargon word 'epigenetic'; under the Code Book numbering those are Q19,Q21,Q23,Q24,Q27, and they are exactly the five lowest-n items of 18 (n=86,114,105,104,110 vs 128-196 for the other thirteen); 1/choose(18,5)=1/8568 by chance. The rival SI 3 numbering predicts Q26,Q27,Q28,Q30,Q31, whose n are 149,110,177,185,152 -- refuted. Separately, all 18 per-item n reproduce EXACTLY from the raw S5 Table columns of the same name (156,176,190,158,148,86,152,114,128,105,104,166,149,110,177,196,185,152), confirming IRW item Qk is source column Qk with no positional step. Once the numbering is fixed every item is distinguished. NOT established by this route: the option_text<->resp axis (taken from the Code Book's own primary-code column and SI 3's column headers, stated outright, no inference), and what pilot-1 respondents physically read (the administration was in Brazilian Portuguese, unpublished, so the shipped English is a translated_substitute; the two English documents minor wording variants are likewise not adjudicated).

route: explicit code labels (3 documents) + code-is-source-column-name; full source re-run of per-item n and number-correct; truth-class pinning; route 8 semantic complements/difficulty coherence
evidence: Route: explicit code labels in three source documents + core-model-3 'code IS the source column name', corroborated by a full re-run of the processing script's scoring against the live data and by semantic-complement structure. (1) The pilot-2 raw file's columns are literally Q1..Q9 and data/carver_2017_puggs_items.py melts them unrenamed, so there is no positional step. The questionnaire prints its own item numbers 1..9 beside each stem, S2 Table lists the same numbers with the same wording, and the pilot-2 Code Book keys 'Question 1 (Q1)'..'Q9'. (2) Re-running the script's rule (keep raw in {1,2}; resp = raw == key) over source columns Q1..Q9 reproduces the live per-item n AND the live per-item number correct for all 9 items exactly: n = 66/68/65/55/66/71/66/73/53 and k = 23/64/52/38/44/66/47/68/28 (p = .35/.94/.80/.69/.67/.93/.71/.93/.53), 583 rows. No item sits at 50% correct (closest is Q9, 28 correct of 53), so flipping any single item's key would change that item's k -- the data therefore pin each item's keyed truth value, splitting the block into True-keyed {Q3,Q5,Q8,Q9} and False-keyed {Q1,Q2,Q4,Q6,Q7}. (3) Every shipped stem is scientifically consistent with its item's data-pinned truth value, 9 of 9, and matches the truth value S2 Table independently prints beside the same item number, 9 of 9 -- so no permutation across the two truth classes is possible. (4) Semantic complements: the only two items sharing the referent 'A person's height' (Q4 'one gene only', Q9 'many different genes') are mutually the most negatively correlated pair for each other at r = -0.572, and the 'Most traits and diseases are caused by ...' complements Q2 (a single gene) and Q8 (both genes and environmental factors) likewise at r = -0.734, the strongest value in the matrix. Difficulty coheres with content: the two polygenicity items are the hardest (Q9 p=.53, Q5 p=.67) and the gene-and-environment items the easiest (Q2 .94, Q6 .93, Q8 .93), which a Q5/Q8 swap would invert. (5) Pilot boundary: the pilot-2 raw file has 45 Q + 17 TT columns and S1 Table numbers 45 items with 17 traits, while pilot 1 has 51 + 20 and covers this construct with 13 Likert items; no pilot-1 material was used. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: the statistics alone do not separate Q1, Q6 and Q7 from one another within the False-keyed class -- only difficulty plausibility speaks to those (Q1 p=.35 as the flagship determinism misconception, Q6 p=.93 as the obviously wrong 'environmental factors only'). Their identity rests on the printed item numbering, which is a label match carried by three source documents and by the data column names rather than an order inference, which is why the status is VERIFIED rather than PARTIAL. Also checked and NOT reproduced: the paper's one published pilot-2 per-item figure, '78.8% correct' for the single-gene item, against Q2's 82.1% (64/78, don't-know and missing in the denominator -- the convention that reproduces the paper's pilot-1 figures for the same item exactly, 26.6% vs '26%' and 19.3% vs '19.3%'). No Section-3 column reproduces 78.8% under any convention tried, so it discriminates nothing either way.

route: explicit code labels + code-is-source-column-name; full source re-run reproducing per-item n and number-correct (16/16 exact); route 8 semantic coherence of the don't-know pattern
evidence: Route: full source re-run of the correctness recoding (core model 3 'code IS the source column name' + the explicit-code-label exemption), corroborated by route 8. (1) The pilot-2 raw file (S6 Table, s006.xlsx) has columns literally named Q10..Q25 and data/carver_2017_puggs_items.py melts them unrenamed, so there is no positional step. (2) Recomputing, from that xlsx, resp = (raw == Code-Book key) after dropping raw 3 (don't know) and 99 (missing) reproduces the live per-item (n, number correct) for ALL 16 items EXACTLY -- Q10 54/12, Q11 65/51, Q12 70/58, Q13 54/34, Q14 51/21, Q15 35/21, Q16 56/29, Q17 46/34, Q18 42/29, Q19 49/15, Q20 50/19, Q21 52/14, Q22 40/16, Q23 60/51, Q24 62/52, Q25 56/38 (live counts from a server-side GROUP BY, no export). Because resp is a correctness score, (n, k) is a joint fingerprint of BOTH the column identity and the key direction: flipping any one item's key sends k -> n-k, and n != 2k for every one of the 16 items (the flipped k would be 42,14,12,20,30,14,27,12,13,34,31,38,24,9,10,18 -- different from the observed k in all 16 cases), so no single-item key error and no permutation of items is consistent with these numbers. This distinguishes every item from every other. (3) Text-to-code: S1 Table prints the item number 10-25 beside each stem and S2 Text labels the same block Q10-Q25 under the same section heading, so item_text is tied to the code by a label match rather than an order inference. (4) Corroboration (route 8): the five statements whose text mentions 'epigenetic' (Q15, Q17, Q18, Q19, Q22) are exactly the five items with the lowest n, i.e. the most don't-know/missing (35, 46, 42, 49, 40 of 78; next lowest is Q20 at 50), matching the paper's own report that the epigenetics items drew by far the most 'Don't know' answers. A permuted text-to-code assignment would not put the epigenetics stems on the five sparsest columns. (5) Key independence: the key is the pilot-2 Code Book's (S2 Text), and it also agrees item-for-item with the scientific truth value of each statement; the raw file's own Sheet2 key was NOT used, since it covers only questions 1-9 and mislabels its last row 'Question 10' (the data reject that row's direction for Q10). WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: (a) that the shipped English is the wording pilot-2 respondents actually read -- the administration was in Brazilian Portuguese and no Portuguese text exists anywhere in the deposit, so the base fields are an English substitute (language=Portuguese, _translated empty); (b) that S1 Table's wording is byte-identical to the form used in the second pilot rather than a lightly copy-edited final version -- the paper places both revisions before the second pilot and reports 45 final items (matching), and S1 still carries the 'Don't know' column the authors say they removed after the pilots, but the Code Book publishes no stems, so there is no second copy of the pilot-2 wording to diff against; (c) nothing about the option level -- resp is 0/1 correctness, option_text is blank by design, so there is no option-to-resp mapping to verify.

route: Step 5b exemption (explicit code labels in the source: the released page prints the item's unique ID) + core-model-3 pattern-1 code derivation; re-checked against CDM iteminfo response_options and the released sets' printed Keys -- see verify_cdm_timss03.R
evidence: The code-to-wording tie is a printed unique-ID match, item by item, which distinguishes every item from every other. data/cdm.R takes the IRW code straight from the source column name (grep('^M', names(x)) over CDM::data.timss03.G8.su$data, item = names(x)[i]) -- pattern 1 of core model 3, nothing to get wrong -- and those column names are IEA TIMSS unique item IDs. Every released page prints that ID in its header ('UniqueID M012001', 'Item ID M022234B'), so each item's wording was read off a page carrying its own code rather than inferred from order. verify_cdm_timss03.R re-checks that from two sources that were not used to build the CSV. (1) Shipped item set == the 23 ^M columns of the CDM data frame: identical. (2) Shipped option-row count per item == CDM iteminfo$response_options, a column that ships with the package and was never consulted while transcribing: 22 of 22 agree (5,4,4,4,5,4,5,5,5,5,4,5,4,5,5,4,5,0,0,5,4,4), with M022043 excluded because its five options are pictures and were not transcribed. (3) Shipped correct_response == the answer Key printed in the released sets' own index tables, re-parsed from the PDFs at run time: 23 of 23 agree, including 'See scoring guide' (i.e. blank) for the two constructed-response items M022232 and M022234B, and all 23 codes are found in a released set. Checks 2 and 3 are independent per-item signatures that a permutation of item_text across items would break for most items. What this does NOT establish: the transcription itself is an image read (the released item content is rasterised; pdftotext yields only header metadata and the copyright watermark), so wording and punctuation are OCR-class and warrant a human spot-check, and the bracketed figure descriptions are IRW's own words, not IEA's. It also does not verify the option-to-score direction beyond the printed Key: resp=0 is many-to-one over distractors and omissions.

route: Explicit code label in the source (exemption), corroborated by route 2 (per-item structural signature: block membership x booklet design)
evidence: Every one of the 25 live item codes is printed as its own page header ("Item ID M041052", ...) directly above that item wording in the IEA TIMSS 2007 Grade 4 mathematics released-items PDF, so each item is individually tied to its text by a printed label rather than by position; a permutation is impossible without the header contradicting the page. Corroboration from the data: the same PDF states each item block, and the 14 block-M04 items are answered only in booklet 4 (n=344 each) while the 11 block-M05 items are answered in booklets 4 and 5 (n=698 each) -- reproduced for 25/25 items, with booklet 5 answering exactly the 11 block-M05 items and no others (verify_cdm_timss07.R, run against CDM 8.3.14 data.timss07.G4.lee). route: explicit code labels (Step 5b exemption) + route 1 per-item published statistics + per-item n reproduction against the source object
evidence: Check 1: all 174 live per-item n from irw::irw_table_sets(per_item=TRUE) equal the per-item non-missing n of CDM::data.timss11.G4.AUT[, as.character(q.matrix1$item)] exactly, 0 mismatches, and the item sets are identical -- the live table is that source object column for column, and data/cdm.R assigns item = column name with no positional step. Check 2: each released item's wording was transcribed from the PDF page headed with that item's own IEA ID, and IEA's published Austria percent correct matches the observed percent correct for that column across all 73 released items (Pearson r = 0.9991, mean |diff| 0.82pp, max |diff| 2.2pp against a 3.0pp tolerance; published are survey-weighted, observed unweighted). PARTIAL, not VERIFIED, for two reasons stated plainly: (a) 101 of the 174 items are TIMSS secure items and ship no item_text, so nothing is established for 58% of the table; (b) on their own the percent-correct statistics do not separate every item from every other -- all 73 have at least one rival published value within tolerance -- so the individual pinning rests on the item ID printed on each released page, which is a label match, with the statistics as corroboration that the label is the code the data uses.

route: none available -- no item text shipped
evidence: Nothing was shipped, so there is no mapping to verify. Recorded to state what was ruled out rather than let 'couldn't check' read as 'checked'. Route 5 (subscale blocks) was examined and rejected as a mapping route: the 33 Anglais columns do not fall in contiguous subscale order, so it could at most assign items to one of ~7 correlation clusters and never distinguish members within a cluster. Route 3 (published totals) is unavailable: CS1Anglais..CS6Anglais are integer 1-7 single self-concept items, not motivation subscale composites, so they cannot be solved for membership. Route 1 is unavailable: the paper publishes no per-item means, SDs or floor/ceiling percentages; Table 4 reports CTCM-1 item-specific factor-score correlations with grades, suppresses non-significant values, and carries fewer than ten non-blank English entries. Route 2 is unavailable: all 33 items share one 1-7 scale, so range structure is flat.

NOT_NEEDED: mapping_basis=data_labels, and this table qualifies for BOTH of Step 5b's standing exemptions at once. The pilot-2 spreadsheet's own column headers are the item codes AND carry the trait names (TT1_Height, TT4_Colour blindness, TT13_ADHD, TT17_Blood group), and data/carver_2017_puggs_items.py melts them by name with no rename or positional step (core model section 3 pattern 1). So the code IS the source column name, and the codes are self-describing: a permutation is impossible without being self-evident. Corroborated at extraction by validate_items.R --table-sets (17 items, resp 1-5, both sets exact). Note the pilots differ -- pilot 1 has 20 traits under bare TT1..TT20 codes and a 6=don't know option this form drops -- which is what establishes that the 17-trait S1 Text list is pilot 2's instrument.
